steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
A transformer is a neural-network architecture built to model sequences (text, code, audio, etc.) without using recurrence (RNNs) or convolution. Conceptually it has three key ideas:

1. Token embeddings  
   • Each input token (word-piece, byte, etc.) is mapped to a vector.  
   • A position embedding is added so the model knows order.

2. Self-attention layers  
   • Every token looks at every other token in the same sequence and decides “how much should I pay attention to it?”  
   • For each token we create three learned vectors:  
     – Query (Q): what I’m looking for  
     – Key (K): what I contain  
     – Value (V): what I will pass on if selected  
   • Similarity(Q, K) → attention weights (softmax) → weighted sum of V’s gives a new representation for each token.  
   • Multiple heads run this in parallel, letting the model focus on different linguistic relations (syntax, long-range facts, etc.).

3. Feed-forward & stacking  
   • After self-attention, each token’s vector goes through the same 2-layer feed-forward network (with non-linearity & dropout).  
   • Layer-norm and residual (skip) connections wrap both the attention and feed-forward blocks, stabilizing training.  
   • Stacking many such blocks lets the model build deep, hierarchical knowledge.

Encoder vs. decoder  
   • Encoder (BERT) consumes a full sequence using bidirectional self-attention for understanding tasks.  
   • Decoder (GPT) uses masked self-attention so each token only sees earlier ones, enabling left-to-right generation.  
   • “Encoder-decoder” (T5, original Transformer) pairs them for tasks like translation.

Training  
   • Pre-training objectives (masked-token prediction, next-token prediction, etc.) teach general language patterns.  
   • Fine-tuning or prompting adapts the model to specific tasks.

Why it works  
   • Attention lets the model capture long-range dependencies efficiently (O(n²) per layer but highly parallel on GPUs), avoiding the vanishing gradients of RNNs.  
   • Multi-head design and deep stacking provide rich compositional representations of language.

End-to-end: Embed tokens → repeatedly “attend-and-transform” them → produce logits for the next token or task-specific outputs.
